**Finding: COMPLIANT at the preferred position — no redline proposed.**

Section 24 of the Cobalt Cloud agreement already delivers every element of our preferred ASSIGN checklist:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Customer assignment to Affiliate without consent | 24.1 |
| Customer assignment to M&A successor without consent | 24.1 |
| Vendor may not assign without our consent | 24.2 |
| Consent not unreasonably withheld | 24.2 (and 24.3 residual) |
| No Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor | 24.2 |
| No Vendor termination right on our change of control | 24.4 |

Notably, 24.2 is drafted asymmetrically **in our favour** — the Vendor's change of control is itself treated as a transfer requiring our consent, and delegation of material performance is caught too. Section 24.4 goes beyond the checklist by barring suspension, repricing, fee acceleration and service reduction, not just termination, which forecloses the walk-away scenario entirely. Section 13.3 usefully lets licence rights travel with a permitted assignment, and 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for a permitted successor.

Two points fall marginally short of ideal preferred wording but are **not** deviations and are recorded in the rationale only:
- the competitor bar is limited to a *"direct"* competitor and is subject to our own consent — a gate we control, so it cannot be used against us;
- 24.2 frames reasonableness around assignee capability and financial standing, which narrows rather than widens the Vendor's room to argue.

I also confirmed no back-door exit exists elsewhere. The only adjacent termination trigger, 9.2, is mutual, keyed to insolvency rather than change of control, and expressly provides that "a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination" — so it does not undercut 24.4. Searches for repricing, fee-adjustment, competitor and subcontracting language returned nothing that conflicts.

Recommendation: accept Section 24 as drafted. No negotiation capital needs to be spent here.
